data.long_meaning: Himaja is the name of the goddess of the mountain and forests in Hindu mythology. She is believed to protect the mountains, forests, and all the creatures living in them. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'hima' meaning 'snow' or 'cold' and 'jaya' meaning 'victory'. The name Himaja carries the meaning “Goddess Himaja, mountain goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Himaja usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess himaja, mountain goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, protection, and connection to nature

historical_references.reference:
Himaja was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling from around 230 to 245 AD.
She was known for her military prowess and successfully defended her kingdom against several invasions.
One such invasion was from the Ikshvaku king Rudrasimha, who was repelled by Himaja's army.
Sources suggest that she may have been a patron of Buddhism and Jainism.

Another reference to the name Himaja is found in the ancient Indian epic, the Mahabharata.
In this text, Himaja is the name of a lake situated in the forest of Dandaka, in the Indian state of Karnataka.
The lake was believed to be a sacred place, where the gods would come to bathe and perform rituals.
